questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs 1,000 After two successive discounts, it is sold for Rs 600, If the first discount is x% and the second discount is 25%, then what is the value of x?
questions.questionHtml: The marked price of an article is Rs 1,000 After two successive discounts, it is sold for Rs 600, If the first discount is x% and the second discount is 25%, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
Given:

Marked Price (MP) of the article = Rs.1000 

Selling Price (SP) of the article = Rs.600

First discount = x% 

Second discount = 25%

Formula used:

Discount = MP - SP 

SP after discount = MP × (100 - Discount%)/100

Calculation:

SP of the article after the first discount = 1000 × (100 - x)/100 = 10 × (100 - x) 

SP of the article after the second discount = 10 × (100 - x) × (100 - 25)/100 

⇒ 10 × (100 - x) × 75/100 = 600 

⇒ (100 - x) = 600 × 100/75 × 1/10 

⇒ 100 - x = 80 

⇒ x = 20

∴ The first discount percent = 20%

Alternate Method Formulas used:

Discount rate = Discount/MP × 100 

Also, x + y -xy/100 

Second discount = 25%

Total Discount = 1000 - 600 = 400 

Effective rate of discount = 400/1000 × 100 

⇒ 40% 

Effective rate of discount = x + y - xy/100 

⇒ x + 25% - x × 25/100 

⇒ 40% =  x + 25% - x/4 

⇒ 15% = x - x/4 

⇒ 15% = 3x/4 

⇒ x = 15% × 4/3 = 20%

Where ' d ' is discount and ' MP ' is Marked Price

The marked price (MP) is 50% above the CP

According to the question,

90a = 1305

⇒ 100a = 100 × 1305 / 90 = 1450

∴ The cost price of the article is Rs. 1450

questions.question: The successive discounts of 20%, 10% and 8% is equivalent to a single discount of∶
questions.questionHtml: The successive discounts of 20%, 10% and 8% is equivalent to a single discount of∶
questions.solution:
Given:

The successive discount are 20%, 10% and 8%.

Formula:

Successive discount = X + Y - (XY)/100

Where,

X = First discount

Y = Second discount

Calculation:

Successive discount = X + Y - (XY)/100

⇒ 20 + 10 - 200/100

⇒ 28%

Now, again

Successive discount = X + Y - (XY)/100

X = 28%, Y = 8%

⇒ 28 + 8 - (28 × 8)/100

⇒ 28 + 8 - 224/100

⇒ 36 - 2.24 = 33.76%

∴ The single equivalent discount is 33.76%.

Shortcut Trick

One equivalent discount

= 100 – (80/100 × 90/100 × 92/100 × 100) = 33.76%

Loss percentage = (CP - SP)/CP × 100 

Loss percentage = (100 -  96)/100 × 100 = 4%.

∴ The loss percentage is 4%
